issues.legal_issue: Failure to join a proper but non-necessary party to a mortgage enforcement suit does not make the suit unmaintainable or attract the limitation rule for adding a new plaintiff or defendant.
material_facts: The mortgage right was claimed for an undivided Hindu family.
A family member with an interest in the mortgagee right was not joined when the suit was instituted and was added during the appeal, after the limitation period.
The court found that the omitted family member was not a necessary party.
issues.conclusion: The omission did not affect the maintainability of the suit and did not attract section 22 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 22 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, failure to join a proper but non-necessary party does not make a suit unmaintainable or trigger the provision. The Court referred to Guruvayya Gowda and Others v. Dattatraya Anant and Others.

rule.if: mortgage_enforcement_suit and omitted_person_has_interest and omitted_person_is_proper_party and omitted_person_is_not_necessary_party and omitted_person_added_after_limitation

predicates.mortgage_enforcement_suit: The claimant brought a suit to enforce a mortgage.
predicates.omitted_person_has_interest: A person with an interest in the mortgage claim was not joined when the suit was brought.
predicates.omitted_person_is_proper_party: The omitted person had an interest that made them a proper party to the suit.
predicates.omitted_person_is_not_necessary_party: The court determined that the omitted person was not necessary to the suit.
predicates.omitted_person_added_after_limitation: The omitted person was added to the suit after the applicable limitation period had expired.

issues.definition: When a mortgage enforcement suit omits an interested person who is proper but not necessary and that person is added after limitation, the suit remains maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a suit brought by a family manager is representative of the joint family depends on the circumstances, and the failure to describe the plaintiff as manager in the plaint is not decisive.
material_facts: The first plaintiff was the manager of an undivided Hindu family when the mortgage transaction was made.
The suit concerned recovery of a mortgage amount claimed for the family.
The plaint did not describe the first plaintiff as manager, but its allegations showed that the suit was brought on behalf of the joint family.
issues.conclusion: The suit was instituted by the first plaintiff as manager representing the family and was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a suit was instituted by a manager in a personal capacity or as representing the family is determined from the circumstances of the particular case; omission to state the representative capacity in the plaint is not conclusive.

rule.if: family_claim_suit and plaintiff_is_family_manager and plaint_alleges_family_representation and manager_capacity_not_named_in_plaint

predicates.family_claim_suit: The suit seeks relief on a claim said to belong to a joint family.
predicates.plaintiff_is_family_manager: The plaintiff bringing the suit manages the joint family concerned.
predicates.plaint_alleges_family_representation: The plaint's allegations show that the claim is pursued on behalf of the joint family.
predicates.manager_capacity_not_named_in_plaint: The plaint does not expressly describe the plaintiff as acting in the capacity of family manager.

issues.definition: When a family manager brings a suit on a family claim and the plaint alleges that the claim is pursued for the family, the suit is treated as brought for the family even if the plaint does not name the manager capacity.
